claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9110 §9.2.2: "A request method is considered 'idempotent' if the intended effect on the server of multiple identical requests with that method is the same as the effect for a single such request. Of the request methods defined by this specification, PUT, DELETE, and safe request methods are idempotent." POST is neither safe nor listed.

Round 2 run @ stage-2: both "-> 201", same "id":111, line before last "both responses carry the same order id: yes", last line "orders customer 1 gained from the two requests: 1". `cat -A` of the script shows the sed replacement as ^A (byte 0x01), so both extracted ids are the same byte (or empty) and the comparison is always yes, as the lesson's step 2 now warns. meta text now reads "instead of \1" (no control char).

Reasoning statement, not a version-dependent behaviour: identical items occur both in a retry and in a deliberate repeat order, so item comparison cannot separate them. Consistent with the code: PlaceOrderAsync does no item comparison.
